claim_results.summary: FAIL: ownership and scientific ceilings are correctly bounded, but the asserted PR-153 forbidden-input boundary is not cross-bound into the controlling and generated artifacts.
Exact frozen-candidate code and caller review found no correctness, regression, test-adequacy, claim-hygiene, or maintainability defect in the assigned PR-283 open-set response claim.

Frozen-candidate physics/statistics review fails: core whitening, nuisance quotient, rank ladder, equality semantics, replay, and claim ceiling are sound, but the fixed singular-threshold registration can be bypassed to restore a point candidate and two receipt mutation rows overstate non-executed mutants as killed.
Fresh frozen-candidate replay found no harness, portability, receipt, generated-pack, serial-stack, publication-refusal, or historical-acceptance-integrity defect.

findings.statement: PR-283's delta asserts that PR-153 artifacts are forbidden inputs, but PR-153 is absent from the governing spec, publication-policy forbidden_inputs, receipt-generator caveats, and exact generated receipt; therefore the sealed policy does not enforce the asserted PR-153 provenance boundary and the receipt/spec/policy/delta set is not exactly consistent.
assumptions_used: The PR delta's explicit PR-153 prohibition is intended to be a controlling input boundary for this change set, as required by the assignment.
A forbidden-input boundary is enforced only when it is encoded in the governing spec or policy and propagated into the generated receipt, not when it appears only in prose.
counterevidence_refs: docs/PR_DELTAS/pr-283.md:92-93 explicitly states PR-153 artifacts were forbidden and not read or modified.
The strict claim-language command exits zero because it checks forbidden phrasing, not omission of a required forbidden-input identity.
No PR-153 science artifact appears in the frozen candidate's changed-file inventory, which lowers evidence of actual consumption but does not repair the missing enforceable contract.
reproduction: Observe that the only match among these claim/provenance surfaces is docs/PR_DELTAS/pr-283.md:92, while policy forbidden_inputs and the receipt caveats contain PR-151 only.

Run python3 -B scripts/codex_harness/run_pr283_weak_identification.py check and the registered strict claim-language command; both exit zero, demonstrating that current checks do not kill this omission.
unresolved: Whether PR-153 should be removed from the delta instead of added to spec/policy/receipt is an owner decision; either resolution requires regenerating and resealing the candidate because the governing bytes are frozen.

findings.statement: The frozen PR-283 projection accepts any factory-derived relative-singular threshold whose angle and units match the PR-256 report; it does not require the specified PR-283 threshold identity. Replaying the exact same full-rank report with relative singular value 0.005 under threshold 0.001 changes the default WEAKLY_IDENTIFIED abstention into SEPARABLE_CANDIDATE and returns a point response-class candidate, contradicting the fixed/pre-result threshold and mandatory-abstention contract.
assumptions_used: The threshold_contract section of pr283_spec.yaml is the controlling fixed PR-283 operating contract.
A content identity for an arbitrary caller-created contract does not establish preregistration or equality to the specified contract.
Response-class candidate eligibility remains diagnostic-only and is not interpreted as physical source or family identification.
counterevidence_refs: tests/contracts/test_weak_identification.py:503 verifies omission but not alternate singular-threshold identity
reproduction: Build the registered orthogonal full-rank fixture with global amplitude 0.005 and the default 0.01 relative-singular threshold; observe WEAKLY_IDENTIFIED, TYPE_UNIDENTIFIED, candidate null.
Build a factory-derived threshold contract with the same angle 0.2 and units but relative-singular threshold 0.001.
Call source_separation_gate_from_pr256 with the exact same report, classes, covariance, nuisance, and normalizer, then classify the exact same observation.
Observe SEPARABLE_CANDIDATE, RESPONSE_CLASS_CANDIDATE, response-class-local; executable details are in threshold_registration_oracle.json.
unresolved: A compliant fix must bind the projection to a preregistered/fixed threshold contract identity without falsely making the representation-dependent threshold universal.

findings.statement: The generated receipt claims every registered mutation executed and was killed, but MU283-WEAK-AS-SEPARABLE and MU283-WEAK-PRECEDENCE-DRIFT do not execute the registered mutant defects. The first assigns an unused forced candidate and checks unchanged production output; the second runs unchanged production cases and labels their expected abstention as a killed precedence mutant. Therefore the PASS receipt does not satisfy its own execute-and-kill mutation rule.
assumptions_used: The spec's mutation_rule uses execute and killed literally, requiring the intended defect to be activated in an executable path.
A positive control against unchanged production behavior is not mutation execution.
counterevidence_refs: python -B scripts/codex_harness/run_pr283_weak_identification.py check exits 0 and exactly replays the receipt
The other eight mutation rows exercise actual rejected alternate inputs or forged replay fields
reproduction: Inspect _run_mutations lines 731-742: forced_candidate is never injected into classification or gate logic, while killed is derived from the unmodified classified result.
Inspect _run_mutations lines 906-955: far and broad-equivalence classifications run the unmodified weak gate; no after-open-set precedence mutation is injected.
Run the receipt check and inspect its mutations array; both rows nevertheless report executed=true, activated=true, killed=true.
unresolved: Replace these rows with executable mutants or downgrade the receipt language/status; add a real singular-threshold identity/registration mutation covering the reproduced bypass.
